subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic Gateway receive timestamp to agent-visible inbound metadata, and what field name, timestamp format, and SDK boundary should be canonical?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the public field semantics and propagation boundary is an API/product decision that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define a generic receive-time contract
options.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests that prove source timestamp and Gateway receipt timestamp remain distinct.

options.title: Keep timing internal and improve diagnostics
options.body: Expose receive-to-dispatch timing in logs or diagnostics instead of adding agent-visible prompt metadata.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific instrumentation
options.body: Let individual plugins add timing where they need it, accepting less consistent cross-channel latency analysis.

recommendation.title: Define a generic receive-time contract
recommendation.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests that prove source timestamp and Gateway receipt timestamp remain distinct.

likelyOwner.reason: The routing question is closest to the inbound metadata and prompt contract history tied to this owner signal.
